### Text Preprocessing
We extracted webpage's title, headings, and text. We removed urls, emails, digits, punctuation, symbols and converted all the text to lowercase. The text was split into individual words with stop words removed, the words were then lemmatized and words smaller than 3 characters were removed. We used a vector of TF-IDF weights to represent each page and also kept words that appeared in more than 2 pages.
 
### Predictive Models
We used L2 regularized linear support vector machines that were fitted with LiblineaR for the binary and multiclass settings. The data was split with 80% going to training and 20% for testing stratified by m-class label. Then, we used 5 fold cross validation on the training set to find the optimal regularization cost. We chose the highest average accuracy from these values 0.1, 0.3, 1, 3, 10. 1 was best for the binary model and 3 was best for the multiclass model. The final models were refit with these costs and all the labeled data.


### Estimated Prediction Accuracy
On the test set, the binary model achieved an accuracy of 83.6%, sensitivity of 0.832, and specificity of 0.842. With about equal specificity and sensitivity, this implies the model was about as good on both classes. This accuracy is higher than the neural network model we fitted, which achieved an accuracy of 78.5%. The multiclass model achieved an accuracy of 84.1%, macro averaged sensitivity of 0.780, and macro averaged specificity of 0.948. The accuracy overall is comparable to the binary model even with a higher number of categories. However, the lower macro averaged sensitivity value indicates that the model is less reliable with smaller classes.
